HD.rationale: Home Depot is a high-quality franchise with durable scale advantages and a coherent Pro-pivot strategy, but near-term fundamentals are softening. Q1 FY2026 revenue grew +4.8% YoY to $41.77B and beat consensus, yet net income declined -4.2% YoY and EPS diluted fell -4.3% YoY to $3.30 (GAAP). Margins are compressing: operating margin ~11.9% in Q1 2026 vs ~12.9% a year ago, net margin 8.4% vs 9.0%. The balance sheet carries high leverage (liabilities/equity ~6.8x). Cash generation is a bright spot with OCF surging +39.5% YoY to $6.03B. Valuation at 23x PE is at the lower end of its 52-week range (20.3–28.8x) but not deeply discounted given the earnings deterioration. The qual report's 'operating margin above 15%' claim is inaccurate per the quant data (~12%); I weight the quant pack's actual figures. Q2 earnings on Aug 18 is a near-term catalyst (consensus EPS $4.71, marginal YoY growth), but the setup is not compelling enough to drive a strong re-rating given conservative FY2026 guidance (sales +2.5–4.5%, EPS growth up to 4%). The franchise quality and Pro ecosystem depth support a mildly positive lean, but margin erosion, high leverage, and a tough macro backdrop (10Y at 4.71%) cap the score.
key_factors: Q1 FY2026 revenue $41.77B, +4.8% YoY, beat consensus of $41.51B
Q1 FY2026 EPS diluted $3.30 GAAP (adjusted ~$3.43 per sell-side), -4.3% YoY decline
Net income declined -4.2% YoY to $3.29B; net margin compressed to 8.4% from 9.0% prior year
Operating margin ~11.9% in Q1 2026, down from ~12.9% in Q1 2025 (correcting qual report's 15%+ claim)
Operating cash flow surged to $6.03B in Q1 2026, +39.5% YoY — strong cash conversion
High leverage: total liabilities $94.03B vs total equity $13.87B (debt-to-equity ~6.8x)
PE diluted 23.08x as of July 23, 2026, at lower end of 52-week range 20.3–28.8x
Stock price $324.71 on July 23, down -15.6% from 6 months prior ($384.64), 52-week high $426.75
Pro segment now ~half of sales, outperformed DIY in Q1; SRS Distribution acquisition deepens Pro ecosystem
FY2026 guidance conservative: adjusted EPS growth up to 4%, sales growth 2.5–4.5%
Q2 earnings report Aug 18, 2026 — consensus EPS $4.71, marginal YoY growth; near-term catalyst
10-year Treasury yield at 4.71%, Fed Funds 3.63% — elevated rate environment pressures housing demand and valuation multiples
ROIC of 25.4% per Q1 report (from web sources); ROE compressed to 101% from 184% prior year

sources_cited.excerpt: First-quarter fiscal 2026 sales increased 4.8% year over year to $41.8 billion, while Pro sales outperformed DIY demand and big-ticket transactions returned to positive growth.
The company generated a strong 25.4% return on invested capital… Digital sales increased more than 10% year over year, marking the fourth straight quarter of double-digit growth.
HD is set to report its Q2 earnings on Tuesday, August 18, 2026… analysts expect the company to report diluted EPS of $4.71, up marginally from $4.68 in the year-ago quarter.
FY2024 sales of $159.5 billion were roughly double Lowe's revenue. That gap strengthens The Home Depot market share in home improvement retail.
The 2024 SRS Distribution deal deepened its push into contractors and faster service… The SRS deal gives The Home Depot more reach in pro categories tied to roofing, pool, and landscaping jobs.

On July 20, 2026, The Home Depot shares fell more than 1% as rising crude oil prices pushed the 10-year Treasury yield to 4.60%, fueling inflation concerns and weakening the outlook for housing demand.
